newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power holds steady in cool weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power holds steady in cool weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were mostly steady in cool temperatures, although February prices weakened along with natural gas, industry sources said.
Spot trades were said to be thin with utilities reluctant to part with power in the cold weather.
"Right now they (utilities) seem to be hoarding it all to themselves," said one ERCOT marketer.
Temperatures throughout Texas were forecast to reach maximums in the 20s and 30s degrees Fahrenheit Tuesday and Wednesday.
Longer term forecasts called for much below normal temperatures throughout the state from January 12 to 16.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Wednesday was talked steady in the $36.00-40.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, brokers and marketers said.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Wednesday's heavy load hours was notationally assessed steady at $34.00-38.00 per MWh, the sources said.

Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Wednesday were valued lower at $18.50-19.50 per MWh from near $20.00 on Monday, while non-firm delivery during Wednesday's light load hours was notionally pegged lower at $14.00-17.00 from $15.00-18.00 on Monday, the sources said.
February ERCOT power was valued lower at $32.00-32.50 from $32.50-33.50 on Monday, under pressure from lower natural gas futures and cash prices, the sources said.

Separately, Texas Utilities said Tuesday its 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear power unit 2 was expected to resume electricity production Wednesday after shutting on the weekend for the repair of a main feedwater valve.
